To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
by simply changing shape of the holes, the response of porous structures can be tuned and optimal structures for compaction can be obtained.
by changing the shape of pores in a soft and periodic cellular structure we can tune its response to external loading.
the buckling of a 2D soft structure with square holes can be used to tune the mechanical response of the material and that the optimal buckling can be achieved by changing the pore shape.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanical properties of soft porous materials.
the mechanics and design of 2D soft and periodic structures.
the mechanics of soft porous materials and the effect of porosity on the buckling of 2D periodic structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the shape of the pores has a significant effect on the buckling behavior of the structure.
, by changing the pore shape in 2D periodic porous structure, the buckling response of the structure can be tuned.
the buckling response of soft and porous structures is highly dependent on the pore shape.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shape of the hole is an important parameter that should be considered when designing soft structures.

the buckling response of soft structures can be tuned by changing the shape of voids and the optimal response of soft porous structures is a result of a delicate interplay between the elastic properties of the material and the shape of the voids.
the compaction of soft porous structures can be tuned by changing the shape of pores.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by simply changing pore shape, one can design structures with different buckling thresholds and compaction behavior.
the buckling of the solid matrix can be used as a mechanism to design structures that are compactable.
a simple change in the shape of holes can lead to a significant change in the response of soft and porous structures.
